record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Let C be a genus-2 curve over C that admits a maximal degree-7 map psi_1: C -> E_1 to an elliptic curve, so that its Jacobian J_C is (7,7)-isogenous to E_1 x E_2 for a second degree-7 elliptic subcover E_2 and belongs to the locus L_7 in M_2 of genus-2 curves with (7,7)-split Jacobian. Determine the locus L_7 in the moduli space M_2 of genus-2 curves, and determine the relation between the elliptic curves E_1 and E_2 in each case.

evidence.quote: For our purposes, Ln will simply be the locus of genus 2 curves whose Jacobian is (n, n)-isogenous to a product of two elliptic curves.
Problem 1. Determine the locus Ln in M2 for n = 7. Further, determine the relation between the elliptic curves E1 and E2 in each case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex numbers. Let $\mathcal{M}_2$ denote the coarse moduli space of smooth projective curves of genus $2$. For an integer $n\ge 2$, define the locus
$$L_n \;=\; \{\,[C]\in \mathcal{M}_2 \;:\; \text{the Jacobian } J_C \text{ is } (n,n)\text{-isogenous to a product } E_1\times E_2 \text{ of two elliptic curves}\,\},$$
where an $(n,n)$-isogeny means an isogeny $J_C \to E_1\times E_2$ whose kernel is isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$ and is isotropic with respect to the Weil pairing induced by the principal polarization on $J_C$. Equivalently, $[C]\in L_n$ if and only if there exists a degree-$n$ maximal cover $\psi_1:C\to E_1$ to an elliptic curve $E_1$ (so that $\psi_1$ does not factor through a nontrivial isogeny of elliptic curves), in which case a complementary degree-$n$ elliptic subcover $\psi_2:C\to E_2$ is determined up to isogeny.

Take $n=7$.

(a) Determine $L_7$ explicitly as an algebraic subvariety of $\mathcal{M}_2$, e.g.\ by giving defining equations for $L_7$ in terms of the Igusa invariants $(J_2,J_4,J_6,J_{10})$ of genus-$2$ curves.

(b) For each point $[C]\in L_7$, determine the relation between the two degree-$7$ elliptic subcovers $E_1$ and $E_2$, e.g.\ a parametrization of the pair $(j(E_1),j(E_2))$ and the modular relation satisfied by their $j$-invariants.
artifact.status_search_result: Explicit algebraic descriptions of the locus $L_n$ in $\mathcal{M}_2$ of genus-$2$ curves with $(n,n)$-split Jacobian are known classically for $n=2$ and by Shaska–Völklein/Shaska for $n=3,5$. Survey and later sources indicate that for $n=7$ (and $n>3$ more generally) explicit equations of $L_n$ together with the relation between the two elliptic subcovers have not been computed; the problem is identified as open in computational genus-$2$ literature. Partial computations (Humbert surface of discriminant $49$, pairing-friendly constructions) exist but do not give the full answer requested.

status_evidence.title: The arithmetic of genus two curves (Shaska)
status_evidence.snippet: Shaska dealt with the cases n = 5, 7 ... For n > 3, equations of L_n have not yet been (fully) computed.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit equations for L_7 are not (fully) computed; case n>3 is more difficult.

status_evidence.title: Genus 2 curves with given split Jacobian (Scholten et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses constructions of genus-2 curves with split Jacobian and related Humbert surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Construction-level results, no closed-form description of L_7.
